title: Silas and the Room
premise: Astrid Coldharbour is hired to survey Marrow House, a derelict property whose measurements refuse to stay constant, and whose cellar conceals a door sealed from the inside — a door the 1974 excavation crew buried along with a boy named Silas, taken as payment for a debt the town owed. As Astrid documents the house's impossible geometry, she discovers the frost on its windows writes ledgers: names, dates, and what each resident stole. To survive, she must trace the descendants of those who profited from Silas's disappearance and return what was taken before the winter solstice, when the room finishes counting and comes to collect in full. She succeeds only partially — justice outside the law is never clean — and ends by sealing herself into the record, becoming both witness and payment.
about_author: Zephyrine Voss is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent eleven years cataloguing condemned properties across the northern counties before turning to fiction. They write in unheated rooms, claiming the cold improves their sentence structure.

chapters.title: The House That Measures Back
chapters.summary: Astrid arrives at Marrow House to conduct a pre-demolition survey, armed with laser measures and a habit of documenting everything. The rooms return different dimensions each time she checks. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: Frost Ledger
chapters.summary: Overnight frost forms on every window in patterns too regular to be natural — columns of names and figures. Astrid photographs them; by morning the photos show only her own reflection, smiling when she wasn't. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the first true fear.

chapters.title: Chain of Title
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Astrid finds the deed history riddled with gaps — every owner between 1974 and 1981 struck through in red ink no clerk remembers applying. An elderly archivist goes pale at the address. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: the sense of being expected.

chapters.title: What the Crew Found
chapters.summary: Astrid tracks down Tom Ellery, last surviving member of the 1974 excavation crew, who confesses they unearthed a door sealed from the inside and were paid to rebury it. He gives her a brass key he was told to throw in the river. POV: Tom, then Astrid. Emotional beat: guilt passed like an inheritance.

chapters.title: Silas
chapters.summary: Astrid researches Silas Wren, a twelve-year-old listed as 'relocated' in 1974, whose mother drowned herself in the cistern. The house's frost ledger now shows Silas's name at the top, underlined, waiting. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger becoming personal obligation.

chapters.title: The Excavation
chapters.summary: The demolition crew's backhoe strikes the door. It opens inward before anyone touches it, exhaling air that smells of pencil shavings and snow. One worker walks toward it, smiling, and has to be dragged back. Work halts. POV: crew foreman Dana. Emotional beat: collective dread breaking the crew apart.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Inside the threshold room, Astrid catalogs objects that don't belong to any era: a child's shoe, a surveyor's chain, a jar of teeth, all tagged with paper labels in her own handwriting. Documentation becomes prayer; prayer becomes summons. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: complicity dawning.

chapters.title: The Beneficiaries
chapters.summary: Following the ledger's arithmetic, Astrid identifies four families whose fortunes rose after 1974 — land grants, forgiven debts, a sudden inheritance. Each received something the night Silas vanished. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: righteous anger sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: First Return
chapters.summary: Astrid returns a deed to the Halloway family, who beg her to take it back; within hours their son begins sleepwalking toward Marrow House. The room accepts returns but charges interest. POV: alternating Astrid and Mrs. Halloway. Emotional beat: horror at discovering restitution isn't mercy.

chapters.title: Dana's Bargain
chapters.summary: Foreman Dana, desperate to finish the job and save her crew's contracts, offers the room a substitute name from the ledger. The frost rearranges itself, considering. Astrid catches her at the threshold and stops her. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: power offered and refused — barely.

chapters.title: The Second Surveyor
chapters.summary: Astrid finds the 1974 surveyor's field notes hidden in the wall cavity — his final entry reads 'the house appraises me now.' His skeleton sits at a child's desk, still holding a pencil. POV: Astrid reading his notes (epistolary). Emotional beat: recognition of her own trajectory.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: The frost spreads beyond the windows, climbing interior walls in ledger lines. Astrid's own name appears, dated for the solstice. Her documentation — photos, notes, recordings — begins rearranging itself to tell a story she didn't write. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: loss of authorship over her own life.

chapters.title: Wren Descendant
chapters.summary: Astrid locates Silas's only living relative, a great-niece, Ivy, who grew up hearing the house called a curse. Ivy refuses to help until Astrid shows her the frost ledger — where Ivy's name appears beside Silas's, marked 'heir.' POV: Ivy. Emotional beat: inherited grief igniting into resolve.

chapters.title: The Town That Knew
chapters.summary: Astrid confronts the town council's archived minutes: the 1974 'payment' was voted on, recorded, minuted. Justice outside the law was justice inside the meeting hall. Two council descendants threaten her; one quietly slips her a key to the old school records. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: betrayal of the ordinary.

chapters.title: School Records
chapters.summary: In the sealed school archive, Astrid finds Silas's belongings bagged as evidence and never claimed: a harmonica, a marble collection, a letter to his mother he never sent. These, not the deeds, are what the room wants returned. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: tenderness inside horror.

chapters.title: Counteroffer
chapters.summary: The room speaks through frost and found objects, offering Astrid a deal: bring Silas's things and a living heir, and her name leaves the ledger. Astrid realizes it doesn't want restitution — it wants succession. A new keeper. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: understanding the trap beneath the bargain.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Blizzard seals the roads. The Halloway boy vanishes from his bed; Dana disappears mid-shift; the frost ledger shortens, consolidating debts. Astrid and Ivy carry Silas's effects through the storm toward the open door. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: grim determination against the clock.

chapters.title: The Room Remembers
chapters.summary: Inside, the room replays 1974 in frost-light: Silas lured by adults he trusted, the door sealed behind him by hands he recognized. He has been keeping accounts ever since because no one else would. POV: Silas, finally. Emotional beat: the monster revealed as the wronged.

chapters.title: Restitution
chapters.summary: Ivy sings the song from Silas's unsent letter — a lullaby their family shared. Astrid lays out the belongings and reads the town's 1974 minutes aloud, entering the crime into record at last. The ledger burns its pages one by one. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: catharsis through witnessing.

chapters.title: The Price of Balance
chapters.summary: The room cannot simply forgive; something must hold the count. Silas, freed, chooses to go — but the door needs a keeper who documents honestly. Astrid steps forward before Ivy can. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen, not demanded.

chapters.title: Final Entry
chapters.summary: Astrid's last survey notes are found complete and precise, describing a house that no longer exists on any map. Ivy inherits the documentation and the duty of remembering. The frost on her kitchen window spells only: 'paid in full.' POV: Ivy. Emotional beat: mourning braided with peace.

chapters.title: Appraisal
chapters.summary: Years later, Ivy surveys properties for a living and always measures rooms twice. In one basement she finds a door, sealed from the inside, with a brass key hanging beside it and a note in Astrid's hand: 'It only needs watching, not opening.' POV: Ivy. Emotional beat: vigilance as legacy — belonging finally earned.
